Spicy Salmon Rice Muffins

Sushi-inspired nori cups filled with sesame-soy salmon, cooled rice and a spicy mayo drizzle, finished with avocado and black sesame.

Prep
Not listed
Cook
Not listed
Total
30 min
Difficulty
Not listed
Ingredients
5

Ingredients

  • 3 sheets nori paper
  • 1½ cups (260 g) cooked sushi rice, fully cooled
  • Salmon: 1 lb (450 g) skinless salmon, cut into small cubes; 2 tbsp sesame or olive oil; 1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce; 1 tbsp honey; 2 scallions, diced; ½ tsp each garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder, paprika and dried oregano; salt to taste
  • Spicy mayo: ¼ cup (55 g) Kewpie mayo, 2 tsp sriracha and 1 tsp honey
  • To finish: ½ avocado, finely diced; 2 tsp black sesame seeds

Amounts are scaled from 12 original servings. Season to taste.

Instructions

  1. Heat oven to 400°F (200°C). Cut each nori sheet into four squares. Make sure the cooked rice is completely cool.
  2. Toss salmon with oil, soy sauce, 1 tbsp honey, scallions, spices and salt. Marinate up to 4 hours if time allows.
  3. Press about 1 heaping tablespoon of rice into each cup of a 12-slot silicone muffin pan, letting the nori edges rise up the sides. Add 4–5 salmon cubes to each cup.
  4. Bake 15–17 minutes, until the salmon is opaque and cooked through; broil 1–2 minutes at the end for extra color if desired.
  5. Mix the Kewpie mayo, sriracha and 1 tsp honey. Let the muffins cool slightly, then top with avocado, sesame seeds and spicy mayo.

Cook times may vary when changing batch size.
